gloss: to strike down; to attack; to subjugate

definitions.gloss: to strike down; to slay; to defeat in battle
definitions.explanation: To attack and kill or defeat an enemy, especially in a military or historical context. Often implies righteous punishment or vengeance.

definitions.gloss: to subjugate; to launch a campaign against
definitions.explanation: To mount a military expedition to conquer or suppress an enemy force or region.

examples.japanese: {仇|かたき}を{討|う}つために{旅|たび}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: He set out on a journey to avenge his enemy.

examples.japanese: {忠臣蔵|ちゅうしんぐら}は{主君|しゅくん}の{仇|かたき}を{討|う}った{四十七士|しじゅうしちし}の{物語|ものがたり}だ。
examples.english: Chushingura is the story of the forty-seven samurai who avenged their lord.

examples.japanese: {反乱軍|はんらんぐん}を{討|う}つ。
{将軍|しょうぐん}は{大軍|たいぐん}を{率|ひき}いて{賊|ぞく}を{討|う}ちに{向|む}かった。
examples.english: The general led a large army to subjugate the bandits.

examples.japanese: {朝廷|ちょうてい}は{東国|とうごく}の{反乱|はんらん}を{討|う}つため、{征夷大将軍|せいいたいしょうぐん}を{任命|にんめい}した。
examples.english: The imperial court appointed a shogun to subjugate the rebellion in the eastern provinces.

notes:
Distinct from the homophones {打|う}つ (to hit, to strike physically) and {撃|う}つ (to shoot). {討|う}つ specifically means to attack and defeat an enemy, often with a connotation of justice or retribution.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {敵|てき}を{討|う}つ (to strike down the enemy)
- {仇|かたき}を{討|う}つ (to take revenge)
- {賊|ぞく}を{討|う}つ (to subjugate bandits)

RELATED WORDS:
- {討伐|とうばつ} — subjugation, punitive expedition
- {仇討|あだう}ち — revenge, vendetta
- {討論|とうろん} — debate (different usage of {討|とう})

Primarily used in historical and literary contexts. In modern usage, {仇|かたき}を{討|う}つ survives as a set phrase.
